assessments.reasoning: agpl_terms [28300,28957) ties the inclusion sentence to the source offered for the modified version to its interacting remote users. Reading the sentence as an unconditional demand for GPL source would lose both its antecedent and its incorporation condition.

agpl_terms [28959,29400) resolves the preceding sentence's reference to the following paragraph. It specifies GPLv3 and formation of a single work. Sharing a host or distribution medium alone meets neither test for incorporation.

agpl_terms [5264,6955) defines the source needed for the object-code work, including necessary control scripts, and specifies exclusions for System Libraries and qualifying tools. Automatically regenerable material may be omitted. For a source-form work the work itself is its Corresponding Source. These distinctions defeat a reading that requires every file on the host.

challenge.method: Tested whether retaining GPLv3 on a part excuses omitting its source, whether every co-deployed program must be included, and whether §1 alone establishes the specific inclusion.
challenge.results: Retention of GPLv3 on the incorporated part is consistent with including its Corresponding Source in the offer. Independent co-deployment and membership in a §5 aggregate do not by themselves satisfy incorporation. GPLv2-only material lacks the specified GPLv3 grant. Section 1 determines source content, while §13 supplies the express inclusion rule.

limitations: The inclusion sentence depends on both the network-offer conditions and incorporation under the specified route. The records contain no component inventory or source archive.
reasoning: AGPLv3 §13 paragraph one's final sentence specifies the contents of the preceding network offer. When that offer is required, it includes the Corresponding Source of each GPLv3 work incorporated by the single-work route in paragraph two. Section 1 defines what counts as Corresponding Source for the work in question.
